full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.11.2018, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3807 of 2015, making the Rule absolute with cost of TK.5000/- by which the judgment and order dated 16.09.2015, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 07 of 2014, has been set aside and the judgment and order dated 30.10.2013 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 has been affirmed. 

 5. The trial Court after hearing the parties rejected the said application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code by Order No. 14, dated 10.05.1992.- Against which, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule and stay in Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992. During the pendency of the said Rule, defendant No.2 Kashim Uddin died in 2000 leaving behind the respondent Nos. 1 to 7 as his heirs. -Meanwhile Mr. Abu Sayeed. Ahmed, the learned Advocate who filed the said revision had been elevated to the Bench and as such, it was not possible to substitute the said heirs of the deceased Kasirnuddin (defendant-petitioner No.2 of Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992)in the said revision. Ultimately, the said Civil Revision stood abated against the opposite parties on 09.07.2008 and as such, the lower Court record was sent back to the trial Court whereupon the proceeding of the suit was re-started and ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte by judgment and order dated 03.10.2012 against the defendants. Thereafter, on 17.04.2013 the plaintiffs asked the successors of the defendant No.2 to vacate the suit property when they, for the first time, came to know about such ex parte decree. Hence, they filed Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating inter alia that after arrival of the lower Court record the plain-tiff-respondent Nos. 1 to 7 did not take any step for bringing the legal representatives of the deceased defendant No.2 on record and as such the ex parte decree dated 03.10.2012 would be a nullity as the same has been passed against a dead person. 

 6. The plaintiffs contested the Miscellaneous case by filing written objection contending inter that the defendant No.2 was not a contesting defendant and as such there was no necessity to substitute his legal heirs in his place and as such the successors of the defendant No.2 have no locus standi to file the application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex parte decree. Thus, there is no ground to interfere with the ex parte decree. 

 7: The trial Court after hearing the parties allowed the miscellaneous case and set aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated 03.10.2012 and thereby restored the suit to its original file and number by judgment and order dated 30.10.2013. Against which, the plaintiffs preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 7 of 2014 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was ultimately heard and allowed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, by judgment and order dated 16.9.2015 and set aside the judgment and order dated 30.10.2013, passed by the trial Court in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013. 

 9. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 15.11.2018, upon setting aside the judgment and order dated 16.09.2015 passed by the lower appellate Court and consequently affirming the judgment and order of the trial Court passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 and thereby restoring the original suit to its file and number and directed the heirs of the defendant No.2 to deposit TK.5,000/- as cost to the Chairman, District Legal Aid Committee, Dhaka within 15 days from the date of receiving the order. In the said order the trial Court was directed to give opportunity to the substituted heirs of defendants to file written statement within a reasonable time and dispose of the suit, in accordance with law, expeditiously, within 1 year from the date of receipt of the order. 

 11. Mr. Serajur Rahman, the learned Advocate-On Record, appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the heirs of the late defendant No.2, i.e. the petitioners of Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2013 had knowledge of Civil Revision No. 1247 of 1992 from the very beginning and N-10 notice was issued after Mr. Abu Sayeed Ahmed, the learned filing Advocate of the said revision was elevated to the Bench but no step was taken by them for substitution for which the plaintiff petitioners are not responsible, as such the High Court Division and the trial Court failed to appreciate this aspect while passing the judgments. He further submits that the Miscellaneous case was not maintainable and the same is barred by limitation and that they had no locus standi to file the same and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
